name: Cathinone
effects: The parent compound of the whole cathinone class — amphetamine with a ketone at the β-position
Natural khat (Catha edulis) alkaloid; the leaf's fresh-cut potency is cathinone decaying to cathine
Roughly amphetamine-like but shorter and less potent — the β-keto group is polar and slows brain entry
Plasma half-life 1.5 ± 0.8 h after khat chewing; partly metabolized to norephedrine
US Schedule I and UN 1971 Schedule I; sold on RC markets under the code name 2-PA

mechanismOfAction.summary: Substrate-type releasing agent at DAT and NET, weak at SERT — the β-keto analogue of amphetamine.
mechanismOfAction.description: Cathinone is transported into the neuron by DAT/NET and reverses the transporter, driving dopamine and noradrenaline efflux in the same manner as amphetamine. The β-keto substituent raises polarity and lowers blood-brain-barrier permeability, which is why the same intrinsic releasing potency reads as a weaker, shorter subjective effect. Serotonergic release is minor, so the profile is stimulant rather than entactogenic. Natural khat contains the (S)-(−) enantiomer, the more active of the two.
